description: The admin ACTION surface on the backend: /admin/* routes gated by the RBAC matrix and written to the admin audit trail, delivering the user's two asks (reset-to-onboarding and archive a bot's memory/data) PLUS the governance read/control routes the console needs. Every gated action: (1) re-derives the caller from the verified token and re-checks membership state (govern.guard_principal -- the pull-based offboarding cut) and the org kill switch (govern.assert_not_frozen), (2) checks the specific directory.Capability (RBAC negative fires BEFORE any state change), (3) performs the action, (4) writes a govern.admin_audit_event row (audit-first where a partial failure could hide the action). Reset and archive are modelled on existing modules (onboarding, memory.revoke) and MUST preserve audit/evidence -- never a destructive delete of evidence.
steps: Port the directory-management admin routes from origin/feat/admin-governance-layer's services/handlers/api.py against the re-integrated main (see `git show origin/feat/admin-governance-layer:services/handlers/api.py`, the '--- admin governance ---' block ~line 832 and its helpers ~line 866+): GET /admin/directory (list roster, gated READ_AUDIT_LOG), POST /admin/directory/invites (INVITE_USERS), POST /admin/directory/{subject}/suspend (TERMINATE_COMPUTER, last-Owner guard), POST /admin/directory/{subject}/reactivate (INVITE_USERS), PATCH /admin/directory/{subject} (INVITE_USERS role change), GET/POST /admin/killswitch (status / set, CHANGE_ORG_POLICIES), GET /admin/audit (READ_AUDIT_LOG). Bring the helpers _membership (calls identity.load_membership + govern.guard_principal), _admin_org_id, _member_view, _audit_view, _roster, _apply_member_change (audit-first). Register the parameterized /admin/directory/{subject} routes AFTER the literal ones (invites) as the branch does so ordering is correct. Keep every WHY comment.

Add the RESET-TO-ONBOARDING route: POST /admin/agents/{id}/reset-onboarding. Gate it on directory.Capability.CHANGE_ORG_POLICIES (an org-policy-level action; justify in a comment). Steps inside the handler, after _membership+guard_principal+assert_not_frozen+assert_can: (a) load the agent META row (404 if not this owner's); require it is the entrypoint Bot (agent['entrypoint'] is True) since 'Chief' is the onboarding entrypoint -- reject others with ValidationError; (b) reset agent.systemPrompt to onboarding.brief(agent['name']) via A.plan_update (systemPrompt IS an editable field -- confirm in agents.EDITABLE) so the next run's is_brief() is true again; (c) clear the dm-<agentId> starter thread's messages: query the thread partition (K.thread_pk('dm-'+agent_id)) for Message rows and delete them, then re-seed a fresh starter greeting Message (starter:True) using onboarding.starter_message(entrypoint=True, operator=...) and refresh the Thread META via threads.touch, mirroring the exact row shapes agents.plan_create builds; do all writes atomically where possible; (d) NEVER delete AUDIT#/evidence rows -- only the dm thread's conversational Message rows and the systemPrompt are reset; (e) write a govern.admin_audit_event. Since 'onboarding.reset' is not in govern.ADMIN_AUDITED_ACTIONS, ADD it to that tuple in govern.py (and 'agent.memory_archived' for the next route) so the action is nameable; keep the tuple's fail-closed 'unknown action raises' property.

Add the ARCHIVE-A-BOT'S-MEMORY/DATA route: POST /admin/agents/{id}/archive-memory. Gate on directory.Capability.TERMINATE_COMPUTER (a destructive-adjacent governance action; justify in comment). Inside, after the standard gates: (a) load the agent (404 if not owner's); (b) archive == REVOKE, never hard-delete: query the agent's memory rows (agent-scope: pk=K.agent_pk(agent_id), memory_sk prefix) and any shared_user rows this agent authored, and for each currently-published row apply memory.revoke() via store.update so is_visible() -> False on the next turn (memory leaves the prompt immediately). Also optionally archive the agent workspace/status by reusing the existing archive path (A.plan_update {'status':'archived'}) if the caller passes a flag -- default to memory-only archive so it is not conflated with agent deactivation; (c) evidence/AUDIT rows are NOT touched (append-only, permanent per docs/architecture/10); (d) write govern.admin_audit_event(org_id, 'agent.memory_archived', actor, before/after counts). Return a summary of how many rows were revoked.

Confirm the error mapping: all these raise directory.Escalation (403 via A.Escalation), govern.Frozen/PrincipalNotActive (403 via PermissionError), A.ValidationError (400), NotFound (404) -- all already mapped in handler(). No new except clause needed; verify.

Add web/src/api.js admin.* wrappers used by FEAT-004: admin.directory(), admin.invite(body), admin.suspend(subject), admin.reactivate(subject), admin.changeRole(subject, body), admin.killswitch(), admin.setKillswitch(body), admin.audit(), admin.resetOnboarding(agentId), admin.archiveMemory(agentId). Mirror the existing `live` object's call(...) style. Add matching demo.js stubs so the console renders against fixtures without leaking demoApi into prod builds.

Port tests/test_admin_api.py VERBATIM from the branch for the directory/killswitch/audit routes (`git show origin/feat/admin-governance-layer:tests/test_admin_api.py`), fixing any monkeypatch that references a symbol that moved on main (e.g. the assert_owner move). Then ADD new behavioural tests for the two new actions: (a) RBAC negative -- a MEMBER-role membership calling reset-onboarding / archive-memory gets 403 AND no state change occurred (systemPrompt unchanged, memory still published, NO admin-audit row written) -- assert the gate fires before any write; (b) reset-onboarding on the entrypoint restores is_brief(systemPrompt)==True, clears then re-seeds the starter greeting, and leaves existing AUDIT/evidence rows intact; (c) reset-onboarding on a NON-entrypoint bot is rejected 400; (d) archive-memory revokes published memory (is_visible->False afterward) while leaving evidence/AUDIT rows present, and writes an 'agent.memory_archived' audit row; (e) a suspended admin (MEMBER# state SUSPENDED) calling any /admin action fails closed (403) via guard_principal before the action; (f) the kill switch, when frozen, blocks these actions (govern.assert_not_frozen). Every test must be one that would FAIL if the enforcement were reverted.
Run the full suite + three build checks; confirm green apart from the 3 pre-existing failures; confirm the web build has grep -c demoApi web/dist/assets/*.js == 0.
acceptance_criteria: /admin/directory (GET/POST invites/{subject} suspend/reactivate/PATCH), /admin/killswitch (GET/POST), /admin/audit (GET), POST /admin/agents/{id}/reset-onboarding, POST /admin/agents/{id}/archive-memory all exist and are each gated on the correct directory.Capability with govern.guard_principal + assert_not_frozen applied first.
reset-onboarding restores onboarding.is_brief(systemPrompt)==True and re-seeds the starter greeting without deleting any AUDIT/evidence rows; it is rejected on non-entrypoint bots.

archive-memory revokes (never deletes) the bot's published memory so memory.is_visible->False next turn, leaves evidence/AUDIT append-only rows intact, and writes an 'agent.memory_archived' admin-audit row.
govern.ADMIN_AUDITED_ACTIONS includes 'onboarding.reset' and 'agent.memory_archived'; an unknown action still raises.

Behavioural tests prove: RBAC negative fires before any state change and writes no audit row; suspended admin fails closed; frozen org blocks the actions; reset/archive preserve evidence. All would fail if enforcement were reverted.
web/src/api.js has the admin.* wrappers with demo.js stubs; prod build leaks no demoApi.
Full suite green apart from the 3 pre-existing failures; infra synth + web build pass.
verification: cd web && npm run build && test -f dist/index.html && test $(grep -c demoApi dist/assets/*.js) -eq 0
findings:
COMPLETED. Committed source-only as c958b9d (6 files, no __pycache__/*.pyc; .agents/ left untracked). Full suite: 1272 passed / 3 failed (only the known tests/test_gaps_api.py trio -- no new failures; +46 tests over the FEAT-002 baseline of 1226). cdk synth exit 0; web build produces dist/index.html with grep -c demoApi dist/assets/*.js == 0.

WHAT WAS DONE:
(1) FEAT-001 had ALREADY re-applied the api.py enforcement cut (imports of `directory as D`, `govern`; `_authorize`/_RBAC_ROUTE_PREFIX; `_principal` with assert_owner removed; A.Escalation/PermissionError->403, ValidationError->400, NotFound->404 mapping). So NO api.py conflict resolution or new except clause was needed -- verified. Added `onboarding` to the `from amazai import (...)` line (it was not imported).
(2) Ported the admin governance route block + all helpers (_membership, _admin_org_id, _correlation_id, _parse_role, _member_view, _audit_view, _roster, _admin_list_members/_admin_invite/_admin_suspend/_admin_reactivate/_admin_change_role, _apply_member_change, _admin_killswitch_status/_set, _admin_audit) VERBATIM from origin/feat/admin-governance-layer:services/handlers/api.py, comments included. `_membership` calls identity.load_membership + govern.guard_principal (no old inline assert_owner assumption). Parameterized /admin/directory/{subject} routes registered AFTER the literal /invites route.
(3) Added the two new actions per the user's ask:
    - POST /admin/agents/{id}/reset-onboarding: gate CHANGE_ORG_POLICIES; requires agent['entrypoint'] is True else A.ValidationError (400); systemPrompt -> onboarding.brief(name) via A.plan_update (systemPrompt IS in agents.PATCHABLE, not EDITABLE -- context named it EDITABLE but the real symbol is PATCHABLE); clears dm-<id> MSG# rows and re-seeds one starter greeting (starter:True) via onboarding.starter_message(entrypoint=True) mirroring plan_create's Message shape; refreshes Thread META via threads.touch; audit LAST ('onboarding.reset'). NEVER deletes AUDIT#/evidence.
    - POST /admin/agents/{id}/archive-memory: gate TERMINATE_COMPUTER; revokes (memory.revoke via store.update, never hard-delete) every currently-published agent-scope MEM# row (filtered entity=='Memory' to skip MEMNS) and shared_user rows the agent authored; audit LAST ('agent.memory_archived') with before/after published counts; returns {revoked, publishedBefore}.
    Both gate ORDER: _membership(guard_principal) -> assert_not_frozen -> assert_can -> act -> audit.
(4) govern.ADMIN_AUDITED_ACTIONS += 'onboarding.reset', 'agent.memory_archived' (fail-closed unknown-action-raises preserved).
(5) IMPORTANT DEVIATION/ADDITION: the ported tests/test_admin_api.py includes TestFreezingFailsBotActionsClosed which asserts orchestrator._drive returns {ok:False, reason:'org frozen'} and FAILs the run on a frozen org. FEAT-001 explicitly did NOT wire kill-switch enforcement into the orchestrator (its findings say so). To make that ported test pass AND to satisfy FEAT-003 acceptance 'frozen org blocks the actions', I added a govern.is_frozen check at the TOP of orchestrator._drive (before budget/tools/model), plus `govern` to its imports. Small, in-scope for the enforcement cut. Verified no regressions in orchestrator/loop tests.
(6) web/src/api.js: added live.admin.{directory,invite,suspend,reactivate,changeRole,killswitch,setKillswitch,audit,resetOnboarding,archiveMemory} mirroring the existing call() style. web/src/demo.js: added a matching demoApi.admin object + ADMIN_MEMBERS/ADMIN_KILLSWITCH/ADMIN_AUDIT fixtures and adminAudit/adminSetState helpers. Confirmed prod build leaks no demoApi.
(7) Tests: ported test_admin_api.py verbatim (its admin_table fixture stubs identity.principal_from_event and binds api.Store to moto; no _provision_harness stub needed for directory routes). Added TestResetOnboarding + TestArchiveMemory. NOTE on the single-tenant seam: org_id == user_id today, so a MEMBER-role RBAC-negative test on the OWNER's Bot must demote the OWNER's OWN MEMBER# row to MEMBER (seed_member(admin_table, OWNER, MEMBER)); seeding a DIFFERENT subject's member row under OWNER's org does not make that subject a member of OWNER's org (their Store keys on their own empty org and they resolve to implicit Owner -> would 404 on the Bot lookup, not 403). Suspended-admin test suspends the OWNER's own seat. The reset audit-intact test asserts OLD agent AUDIT# rows survive as a subset (the systemPrompt change itself appends a new agent.updated AUDIT# row, so the trail grows -- the invariant is old rows preserved, not count unchanged).

ENV NOTES for later features: node/npm at /root/.nvm/versions/node/v18.20.8/bin (prepend to PATH). `grep -c demoApi` returns exit 1 when count is 0 (expected). No password ('Password123!') anywhere. Did NOT push / open PR (orchestrator handles that).

REVIEW-FIX ROUND 1 (commit dbe3cae, backend portion): Addressed review issues #2 and #3 on the backend. (#2 thread reason) Added helper `_with_reason(base, body)` that folds an optional operator-supplied `reason` from the request body into the govern.admin_audit_event `detail` as `<base> (reason: <reason>)`; a blank/missing reason leaves the base detail unchanged. Wired it into _admin_suspend, _admin_reactivate, _admin_change_role, _admin_reset_onboarding, _admin_archive_memory. suspend/reactivate/reset-onboarding now take a `body` param (route dispatch updated to pass it; archive-memory and change-role already had body). The subject/agent id STILL comes from the path only -- only the free-text reason is body-supplied. (#3 gate order) Reordered _admin_reset_onboarding and _admin_archive_memory to guard_principal (via _membership) -> assert_not_frozen -> assert_can, matching the member-write handlers and the documented contract (was assert_can before assert_not_frozen; behaviour was already safe, this is consistency). Added tests/test_admin_api.py::TestOperatorReasonReachesTheAuditDetail (6 tests) asserting the reason lands in the detail for all five actions and that a blank reason leaves the base detail untouched. Frozen-org tests still 403. Full suite 1278 passed / 3 pre-existing failed.

REVIEW-FIX ROUND 2 (commit 58fd6e7): Fixed the single confirmed residual from the second semantic review -- reset/archive buttons sent the owner's user SUBJECT (m.subject) as the {id} path segment, but the server treats {id} as an AGENT id (K.agent_pk lookup); agent ids come from the Bot's slugged name ('chief'), never the subject, so a real console click 404'd. The demo masked it because the stub ignored the id.
  SERVER (services/handlers/api.py): (a) Added `_resolve_entrypoint_agent(store)` -- queries the AGENTS gsi1 index (same as GET /agents) and returns the META of the row with entrypoint is True; raises NotFound ('no entrypoint Bot') if none. (b) Refactored the reset/archive handlers into shared, already-authorized workers `_reset_onboarding_agent(store, agent, body, event)` and `_archive_memory_agent(...)` that take a RESOLVED agent (agent_id derived from agent['agentId']). (c) Added two id-less routes registered BEFORE the parameterized /{id} routes so 'entrypoint' is never captured as an id: POST /admin/agents/entrypoint/reset-onboarding (_admin_reset_onboarding_entrypoint) and POST /admin/agents/entrypoint/archive-memory (_admin_archive_memory_entrypoint) -- both run the SAME gates FIRST (guard_principal -> assert_not_frozen -> assert_can), then resolve the entrypoint server-side from the caller's own org (never the body). The existing /admin/agents/{id}/... routes still work for a known real agent id.
  WEB: web/src/api.js -- resetOnboarding now takes ONLY (reason) and hits the entrypoint route (no id); archiveMemory still takes a real (agentId, reason). web/src/admin/AdminDirectory.jsx -- now loads GET /agents alongside the directory; reset-onboarding is a single button on a new 'Bots' section that acts on the resolved entrypoint (confirm token 'reset'); archive-memory is one button per Bot keyed on that Bot's real agentId. web/src/demo.js -- resetOnboarding resolves the entrypoint from the AGENTS fixture (no id arg); archiveMemory now VALIDATES the agentId against the roster and throws 'no such agent' on a miss, so a regression to sending a user subject fails a test instead of silently passing.
  TESTS: tests/test_admin_api.py::TestEntrypointResolutionRoutes (6 tests) -- seeds an entrypoint agent with name-derived id 'chief', calls the entrypoint route WITHOUT knowing that id, asserts the reset/archive land on it; asserts 404 when no entrypoint; RBAC still gates; and that 'entrypoint' is not captured as an agent id. AdminDirectory.test.jsx -- mocks api.agents, asserts reset is called with ONLY the reason (no id) and archive is called with the picked Bot's real agentId ('worker').
  VERIFY: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -> 1284 passed / 3 pre-existing test_gaps_api failures (no new). web build exit 0, grep -c demoApi dist/assets/*.js == 0. npm test (Node 22) 146 passed. cd infra && npx cdk synth exit 0. A real console click now completes with no 404: reset-onboarding sends NO id (server resolves the entrypoint 'Chief'), archive-memory sends the selected Bot's real agent id.
